newsitem.title: USA: SCATTERED RAIN HIT SOME DRY AREAS OF ILLINOIS-WSC.
newsitem.headline: SCATTERED RAIN HIT SOME DRY AREAS OF ILLINOIS-WSC.

text.p: A few scattered thunderstorms swept across the driest area of west central Illinois Monday night but the coverage was not that high, said Weather Services Corp senior agricultural meterorologist Joel Burgio.
He pointed out that some dry areas in central Illinois and Indiana missed out on much-needed rain during the past 24 hours.
"Thus, the corn crop continues to be under stress in areas that missed the rain," Burgio said.
Elsewhere in the U.S. Midwest Corn Belt, eastern Iowa, parts of northern Illinois and southern Wisconsin got significant rainfall amounts and coverage during the past 24 hours, Burgio said.
For that area, Burgio calculated rainfall of 0.30 to 1.00 inch and locally heavier with 60 percent coverage during the past 24 hours.

During the next 24 hours, the forecast called for a continued chance for scattered showers and thunderstorms from Illinois eastward through Ohio with the best possibility for heavier rains in eastern Illinois and eastward, Burgio said.
He predicted 0.30 to 1.50 inches rain with coverage of 50 to 60 percent for the area during the next 24 hours.
